Delhi is a known and the oldest culture city in the world. The city has its golden past and today is a modern city with old footsteps of great rulers and legends of India, who ruled and nourished this city. This charming city is the capital of India with lots of various traditions, languages, religions and captivating lot of great monuments, museums, parks, & colourful markets. Delhi has been the center of political movement since time immemorial. Delhi is Located in Aravalis mountain range, on its South and North West and River Yamuna on its east. The historical capital of the Pandavas used be called with name of Indraprastha in period of Mahabharata was here found within the stricture of the Purana Qila during 1000 BC. This was in 1000 B.C. The present Delhi is built around the ruins of seven ancient cities. It is said to have been a kingdom of the Gods long before man discovered the city. During a long historical past, the city has faced constant raise and falls, formation and destruction so may time. Delhi was ruled by numbers of Hindu, Mughal, British rulers, the city was always fascination for the conquerors, and emperors.

Delhi is the blend of beauty, charm, complexities, contradictions and dynamism - where the historical past exists with the present. Over 1000 years, it has enthralled plunderers, wooed rulers and tried historians with facts today; the capital preserves an enviable heritage, always on the toe. Delhi remains the center of power, starting with royal influence to colonial power. Today it’s emerging as a significant center for corporate power too. However the city is now can be called truly a cosmopolitan and modern city.

Delhi is the finest amalgamation of an historical past and a pulsating present. Delhi has some of the finest monuments, forts and museums in the country. During 1869 - 1944, the city was declared the capital of India by the British architect Sir Edwin Lutyens. The oriental past can be witness through the buildings left through the centuries, by the invaders. In history the Delhi was ruled during 1060 AD by the Tomar Kings, later conquered by Rajput Chauhans during 12th century, Qutb-ud-din Aibak in 1193 AD. The Mughal ruler Khilji built new capital at Sir- the second city of Delhi, in the city still see around the historical remnants of Khiljis dynasty

Delhi blends an historic past and a vibrant present. Delhi has some of the finest museums in the country. New Delhi was proclaimed the capital of India by the British architect Sir Edwin Lutyens (1869-1944) & is tree-lined & spacious. Legend has it that the Pandavas, the august heroes of the epic Mahabharata, originally founded Delhi, then called Indraprastha, around 1200 B.C. Present day Delhi is built around the ruins of seven ancient cities.

Specifically in 1911 that Delhi recommenced its position and the architects, Edward Lutyens and his architectures; Herbert Baker envisioned their plan to beautify the city. The finest example of their artistic approach are President House and its and adjoining buildings, projecting till today best combination of Indian, English and Roman architecture. The capital used to get shifted between Delhi and Agra during this period, afterwards the British established themselves it was removed to Calcutta.

In the modern city is full of skyscrapers, grand hotels, restaurants, shopping malls. One of posh area of Delhi Connaught Palace which was built in 1931 set the preposition for the development of the city. There is continues redevelopment and growth of the city in nearby suburb and main city. Delhi is economical hub of India and quite prominent in terms of Industrialization, Information, Investments, Science, Technology, Real Estate and Healthcare, etc. Delhi is divided in to 2 divisions, i.e., Old and New Delhi. City Old Delhi is the land of Mughals monuments, mosques and forts all through the old cluttered streets. Old bazaars and authentic food are charm of the old Delhi. Whereas New Delhi is entirely stands apart in terms of lifestyle and city's architecture, built during the British regime. New Delhi is known due to well planed specious markets, roads and landscape with greenery. Important commercial set up is situated in New Delhi's business centres like Nehru Place, Bikaji Kama, Connaught Place, ITI and South Extension. Both New and Old Delhi are quite known as tourists paradise in terms of shopping and sightseeing places, Like Rashtrapati Bhawan, India Gate, Rajghat, Qutab Minar, Humayun’s Tomb, Jantar Mantar, Purana Qila, Red Fort, Jama Masjid, Safdarjang's Tomb and Akshardham temple.

By and large Delhi is a quite multi-linguist and multi-cultured culture and society, which is now flaunting itself to embracing every old and new traditions and cultures. This is said the Delhi is the Queen of All the capital city of India.

Area: 1470 Sq.Km.

Altitude: 239 Mts

Climate: (deg C)-Summer - Max.41.2, Min.21.4, winter - Max.33.7, Min.6.8.,

Languages spoken: Hindi, English and Punjabi

Best Season to visit: September to May.

Places of Interest:

Moghul Monuments: Red Fort, Qutub Minar, Khuni Darwaza, Feroz Shah Kotla, Tughlaqabad, Nizamuddin Aulia, Humayun's Tomb, Lodi's Tomb, Safdarjung's Tomb, Jama Masjid, Jantar Mantar and Red Fort (Son-et-lumiere show).

British Monuments: India Gate, Rashtrapati Bhavan & Mughal Gardens, Parliament House, The Secretariat Complex, Teen Murti House and Connaught Place (Son-et-Lumiere show).

Excursions: Ballabgarh-36.8 kms, Badhkal Lake-32 kms,Dabchick- 92 kms, Karnalake-132 kms, Dasna- 40 kms, Dhanaa- 41 kms, Dharudara-70 kms, Hindon- 19 kms, Hodal- 90 kms, Maur Bund- 32 kms, Okhla-11 kms, Sardhana- 24 kms, Sohna-56 kms and Suraj Kund- 18 kms.

Other Monuments: Ladakh Buddha Vihar, Raj Ghat, The Supreme Court, Shanti Vana, Vijay Ghat, , Bahai’s temple, Vigyan Bhavan, Diplomatic Enclave.

Reach:

By Air: Delhi is well connected by air with all major and A class cities in India.

By Rail: Well connected with all major towns.

By Road: Agra: 204 kms, Jaipur: 260 kms, Almora: 375 kms, Khajuraho: 596 kms, Kullu: 502 kms, Shrinagar: 876 kms, Mathura-147 kms, Mussourie- 269 kms, Nainital-318 kms, Shimla -343 kms, Udaipur-663 kms.

Welcome at Indira Gandhi International Airport on arrival at 7.30 pm at Delhi with a PLA card of your name and transferred by a/c mini coach to the pre-booked hotel. After check in, our representative will hand over all required documents related to the tour and service and brief you about the tour - intercity travel, sightseeing places, stopovers, eating places, local SIM card, money exchange, tips etc., rest of the time for relaxation. Dinner and overnight at the hotel.

Services: Hotel accommodation with dinner and transportation for transfer.

Delhi, the towering capital city of the independent and largest democratic country in the world: India.

Delhi is located and sprawled on both banks of Yamuna River. The city is enriched with culture, architecture and human diversity, Delhi city is a blend of the ancient past of India with the vibration of the modern world. The city designed by the British architect Sir Edwin Lutyens (1869-1944) & is tree- lined & spacious. Legend has it that the Pandavas of epic Mahabharata, the august heroes, founded Delhi around 1200 BC & the name of the city was Indraprastha.

After breakfast take a sightseeing tour of Old Delhi : visiting at Rajghat, the memorial of Mahatma Gandhi, where he was cremated. The sightseeing continues to explore New Delhi: Visiting India Gate; built to honour and pay a tribute to the Indian soldiers who sacrificed themselves during the Afghan war, Birla Mandir (Laxmi Narayan Temple), Lotus shaped Bhai’s Temple, Qutub Minar; built by Qutub-ud- din Aibek of the Slave Dynasty. Later visit to Chattarpur Temple:

dedicated to the goddess Katyayani. The entire complex of the temple is spread over a wide area of 28 hectares. In the evening - visit most famous Swaminarayan Akshardham Temple, 'Akshardham' means the divine abode of God. Showcasing 10000 years of Indian culture in all its breath-taking grandeur, beauty, wisdom and bliss. If time permits optionally, you can attend the Light and Sound show in the temple complex. After visit return to the hotel for dinner and overnight stay.

Services: Hotel accommodation with breakfast and dinner, transportation for sightseeing with guide.

The Akshardham temple , which attracts approximately 70 % of all tourists who visit Delhi, it is the largest Hindu temple after the Akshardham in Gandhinagar both inspired and developed by Pramukh Swami Maharaj, the spiritual head of the Bochasanwasi Shri Akshar Purushottam Swaminarayan Sanstha, whose 3,000 volunteers helped 7,000 artisans construct the temple. Musical fountain Known as the Yagnapurush Kund, it is India's largest step well.

After breakfast check out the hotel and drive to Haridwar, on arrival transfer to the hotel. After relaxation, in the evening attend the most speculative “Ganga Aarti” at the holy River Ganga. Aarti takes place on the ghat in the evening after sunset. A group of Brahmans hold huge fire bowls in their hands and offer their holy mantras to river Ganges, Shiva - the Hindu God of destruction, Surya - the Sun God and the entire Universe. The scenario at Har - Ki - Pauri at the time of Ganga-Aarti is mesmerizing. Afterwards return to the hotel for dinner and overnight stay.

Haridwar: ‘The gateway to the Gods'. \"This place is very beautiful\", at one site one will say so and fall in love with the scenic beauty of the blend of height and plains. In its long history back to pre-historic time, the Haridwar got its name from the rishis. According to the mythology it is known as Kapilsthan, legend goes that the Suryavnshi Prince Bhagirath performed penance here to salvage the souls of his ancestors who had perished due to the curse of the sage Kapila. The penance was answered and the river Ganga trickled forth from Lord Shiva's locks and its bountiful waters revived the sixty thousand sons of King Sagara. Mythologically, drops of nectar churned out from the primordial ocean fell at the four sites of the Kumbh mela including Haridwar.

It is most ideal destinations for meditation, yoga and other aspects of Hinduism. For the adventure seekers, Rishikesh is the suggested place for starting their trekking expeditions to the Himalayan peaks and for rafting. Also, International Yoga Week, which attracts participation from across the world, is held here, every year, in February on the banks of the Ganga.

Mathura and Vrindavan , twin cities in Uttar Pradesh, India, are revered as the land of Lord Krishna's birth and childhood, making them a major pilgrimage destination for Hindus. Mathura is known as Krishna's birthplace, while Vrindavan is where he spent his childhood, playing with friends and engaging in divine pastimes. A trip to Mathura-Vrindavan offers a blend of spiritual experiences, historical sites, and cultural immersion. The notable and most popular sightseeing places and temples are Krishna Janam Bhoomi Temple, Prem Mandir, Banke Bihar Temple, ISKCON Temple, Nidhivan.

Jaipur is widely known as the ‘Pink City’ of India. The walls, houses and buildings of the entire city were washed with pink colour for a grand and royal welcome of Prince Albert and Queen Victoria of Britain, who visited Jaipur in 1853 A.D. This splendid city as was founded in 1727 A.D by one of the greatest ruler Jai Singh II. Jaipur is surrounded by hills on three sides. Jaipur is the only city in the world, which is designed in accordance with Hindu architectural science called Shilpa Shastra. The city had been designed in rectangular shape of 9 blocks, depicting the 9 partitions of the universe. This fascinating city houses - majestic forts, grand palaces, lavish gardens, havelis and museums. While visiting these places you will have a true vision of the royal golden past of Rajasthan.

Chennai (Madras): the capital of the state of Tamil Nadu is the most convenient point of entry for the state. Chennai has an international airport, a seaport, a rail and road network that links it to all major towns and cities of the region. Tamil Nadu is a bastion of Hinduism, whose past endures into the present. Temples with towering spires called gopurams are a common feature of this state, seldom seen anywhere else in the country. Temples in Tamil Nadu were the fulcrums of society and even today art forms that find their origin in religious worship continue to colour daily life. Notable among these are splendid bronzes of deities, glass paintings and Bharatnatyam - an evocative dance form.

Mahabalipuram with its picturesque location on a rocky outcrop between the beach and a lagoon is a happy combination of history, good beaches, hassle-free tourism, fabulous fish and lobster! Despite the many visitors, drawn by the former Pallava dynasty town, the place is friendly, relaxed, and the villagers are remarkably unperturbed by their crowds of visitors. Mahabalipuram is renowned for its series of charming rathas and the spectacular carved relic depicting Arjuna's Penance. The magnificent Shore Temple, built by King Rajasimha in the seventh century, is a unique temple that houses the shrines of both Shiva and Vishnu while the Varaha Cave is one of the many rock-cut caves in Mahabalipuram. The Krishna Mandapam has a relic of Lord Krishna lifting the Govardhan hill in his fingertips.

Kanchipuram is known as one of India's Seven Sacred cities and the historical capital of the Pallavas. It was under the Pallavas from 6th to 8th century A.D and later became the citadel of Cholas, Vijayanagar Kings, the Muslim and the British. It has been a centre of Tamil learning, cultural and religious background for centuries. Kanchi is also known as the centre of the finest silk sarees made in the country. Kanchi has magnificent temples of unique architectural beauty bearing eloquent testimony to its glorious Dravidian heritage. Adi Sankara established his Episcopal seat (Kamakotipeetam) here in the city. The city is also the birthplace of C.N. Annadurai, former Chief Minister of Tamil Nadu affectionately called as \"Anna\" by the people of Tamil Nadu.

The Tirumala Hills are part of Seshachalam Hills range. The hills are 853m above sea level. The Hills comprises seven peaks, representing the seven heads of Adisesha. The temple lies on the seventh peak - Venkatadri, on the southern banks of Sri Swami Pushkarini, a holy water tank. Hence the temple is also referred to as \"Temple of Seven Hills\". Tirupati’s presiding deity; Lord Venkateswara, is famous all over the world as the giver of boons, and is paid homage by people across all religions and races. The Temple is dedicated to Lord Venkateswara, an incarnation of Vishnu, who is believed to have appeared here to

save mankind from trials and troubles of Kali Yuga.

// Blog post (5 Nov 2026): one of the first three posts; its text is changed in the admin panel (Blog). module.exports = { file: 'best-time-to-visit-india.html', url: '/blog/best-time-to-visit-india', heading: 'Best Time to Visit India: A Season-by-Season Guide', category: 'Travel tips', date: '2026-11-05', author: 'Meruka India Tourism', excerpt: 'India has three main seasons, and each part of the country is at its best at a different time. Here is when to go where, so your private tour meets the best weather.', photo: '/photos/taj-mahal-feature.webp', html: '

India is a big country with very different weather from north to south. There is no single “best month” for everyone, but there is a best time for each region. Here is a simple guide to plan your private tour.

' + '

Winter: October to March

' + '

This is the main travel season for most of India. Days are sunny and pleasant, and nights are cool in the north.

' + '
  • Golden Triangle (Delhi, Agra, Jaipur): perfect for sightseeing; carry a warm layer for December and January mornings.
    • ' + '
  • Rajasthan: forts, palaces and the desert at Jaisalmer are best in these months.
    • ' + '
  • Kerala and South India: dry and green, ideal for the backwaters and beaches of Goa.
' + '

Summer: April to June

' + '

The plains get very hot, so this is the time to go up into the mountains.

' + '
  • Ladakh, Himachal and the hill stations of the north are open and cool.
    • ' + '
  • Darjeeling and Sikkim in the east have clear spring days.
' + '

Monsoon: July to September

' + '

The rains bring green landscapes and fewer travellers. Kerala is lovely for Ayurveda in this season, and Ladakh stays dry because it lies beyond the rains.

' + '

Our tip

' + '

Book early for the peak weeks of December and January, when the best hotels fill first. Tell us your dates on Plan My Trip and we will suggest the right route for that time of year. See also Best Time to Visit.

', title: 'Best Time to Visit India: A Season-by-Season Guide — Meruka India Tourism', description: 'When to visit India: the best months for the Golden Triangle, Rajasthan, Kerala, Ladakh and the hill stations, season by season.', keywords: 'best time to visit India, India weather, India travel season', breadcrumb: [{ label: 'Home', href: '/' }, { label: 'Blog', href: '/blog' }] };

// Blog post (5 Nov 2026): one of the first three posts; its text is changed in the admin panel (Blog). module.exports = { file: 'golden-triangle-first-trip.html', url: '/blog/golden-triangle-first-trip', heading: 'Delhi, Agra and Jaipur: Your First Golden Triangle Tour', category: 'Destinations', date: '2026-10-28', author: 'Meruka India Tourism', excerpt: 'The Golden Triangle is the classic first trip to India. Three cities, the Taj Mahal and the forts of Rajasthan, all in about a week with your own car and driver.', photo: '/photos/jaipur-hawa-mahal.webp', html: '

The Golden Triangle joins three of India’s great cities: Delhi, Agra and Jaipur. The drives between them are short, so you see a lot without rushing. That is why it is the favourite first tour for our guests.

' + '

Delhi: old and new

' + '

Start with Old Delhi: the Red Fort, Jama Masjid and a rickshaw ride through Chandni Chowk. In New Delhi, see Humayun’s Tomb, Qutub Minar and India Gate.

' + '

Agra: the Taj Mahal

' + '

Plan to see the Taj Mahal at sunrise, when the marble glows and the crowds are small. Agra Fort and the “Baby Taj” complete the day. Note that the Taj Mahal is closed on Fridays.

' + '

Jaipur: the Pink City

' + '

Visit Amber Fort, the City Palace, Jantar Mantar and the Hawa Mahal. Jaipur is also the best place for textiles, gems and blue pottery.

' + '

How many days?

' + '
  • 5 to 6 days covers the three cities comfortably.
    • ' + '
  • 7 to 8 days lets you add Ranthambore for tigers or Varanasi on the Ganges.
    • ' + '
  • Want more? Add Udaipur and Jodhpur for a longer Rajasthan tour.
' + '

Travel privately

' + '

Every Meruka tour is a private tour, with no sharing: your own car, driver and local guides, and hotels you choose. See our Golden Triangle tours or plan your own trip.

', title: 'Delhi, Agra and Jaipur: Your First Golden Triangle Tour — Meruka India Tourism', description: 'Plan your first Golden Triangle tour of India: what to see in Delhi, Agra and Jaipur, how many days you need and how to add Ranthambore or Varanasi.', keywords: 'Golden Triangle tour, Delhi Agra Jaipur, Taj Mahal tour, first trip to India', breadcrumb: [{ label: 'Home', href: '/' }, { label: 'Blog', href: '/blog' }] };

// Blog post (5 Nov 2026): one of the first three posts; its text is changed in the admin panel (Blog). module.exports = { file: 'india-festivals-holi-diwali.html', url: '/blog/india-festivals-holi-diwali', heading: 'Holi, Diwali and More: Planning a Trip Around India’s Festivals', category: 'Festivals', date: '2026-10-20', author: 'Meruka India Tourism', excerpt: 'Seeing a festival is one of the best memories of an India trip. Here are the big ones, when they fall and how to plan your tour around them.', photo: '/photos/holi-festival.webp', html: '

India celebrates something almost every month. A festival brings streets to life with music, colour, lights and food, and it lets you see the country as Indians enjoy it. Here are the festivals our guests love most.

' + '

Holi: the festival of colours (March)

' + '

Holi welcomes spring with coloured powder, water and dancing in the streets. Mathura and Vrindavan near Agra hold the most famous celebrations, and Jaipur and Udaipur are lovely too. Wear old clothes and keep your camera in a plastic cover.

' + '

Diwali: the festival of lights (October or November)

' + '

Homes, temples and markets glow with oil lamps and fireworks. Jaipur’s bazaars are lit up beautifully, and Varanasi celebrates Dev Deepawali on the ghats two weeks later.

' + '

Pushkar Camel Fair (November)

' + '

Thousands of camels, traders and pilgrims meet at the holy lake of Pushkar in Rajasthan, with races, music and a colourful fair.

' + '

Other favourites

' + '
  • Hemis Festival in Ladakh (June or July): masked dances at the monastery.
    • ' + '
  • Onam in Kerala (August or September): snake-boat races and flower carpets.
    • ' + '
  • Hornbill Festival in Nagaland (December): the tribes of the North-East in one place.
' + '

Plan ahead

' + '

Festival dates follow the Hindu calendar and change every year, and hotels fill early. Tell us which festival you would like to see on Plan My Trip, and we will build your private tour around it. More in Fairs & Festivals.

', title: 'Holi, Diwali and More: Planning a Trip Around India’s Festivals — Meruka India Tourism', description: 'India’s best festivals for travellers — Holi, Diwali, the Pushkar Camel Fair, Hemis, Onam and Hornbill — and how to plan a private tour around them.', keywords: 'India festivals, Holi tour, Diwali in India, Pushkar Camel Fair', breadcrumb: [{ label: 'Home', href: '/' }, { label: 'Blog', href: '/blog' }] };

Delhi is a known and the oldest culture city in the world. The city has its golden past and today is a modern city with old footsteps of great rulers and legends of India, who ruled and nourished this city. This charming city is the capital of India with lots of various traditions, languages, religions and captivating lot of great monuments, museums, parks, & colourful markets. Delhi has been the center of political movement since time immemorial. Delhi is Located in Aravalis mountain range, on its South and North West and River Yamuna on its east. The historical capital of the Pandavas used be called with name of Indraprastha in period of Mahabharata was here found within the stricture of the Purana Qila during 1000 BC. This was in 1000 B.C. The present Delhi is built around the ruins of seven ancient cities. It is said to have been a kingdom of the Gods long before man discovered the city. During a long historical past, the city has faced constant raise and falls, formation and destruction so may time. Delhi was ruled by numbers of Hindu, Mughal, British rulers, the city was always fascination for the conquerors, and emperors.

Delhi is the blend of beauty, charm, complexities, contradictions and dynamism - where the historical past exists with the present. Over 1000 years, it has enthralled plunderers, wooed rulers and tried historians with facts today; the capital preserves an enviable heritage, always on the toe. Delhi remains the center of power, starting with royal influence to colonial power. Today it’s emerging as a significant center for corporate power too. However the city is now can be called truly a cosmopolitan and modern city.

Delhi is the finest amalgamation of an historical past and a pulsating present. Delhi has some of the finest monuments, forts and museums in the country. During 1869 - 1944, the city was declared the capital of India by the British architect Sir Edwin Lutyens. The oriental past can be witness through the buildings left through the centuries, by the invaders. In history the Delhi was ruled during 1060 AD by the Tomar Kings, later conquered by Rajput Chauhans during 12th century, Qutb-ud-din Aibak in 1193 AD. The Mughal ruler Khilji built new capital at Sir- the second city of Delhi, in the city still see around the historical remnants of Khiljis dynasty

Delhi blends an historic past and a vibrant present. Delhi has some of the finest museums in the country. New Delhi was proclaimed the capital of India by the British architect Sir Edwin Lutyens (1869-1944) & is tree-lined & spacious. Legend has it that the Pandavas, the august heroes of the epic Mahabharata, originally founded Delhi, then called Indraprastha, around 1200 B.C. Present day Delhi is built around the ruins of seven ancient cities.

Specifically in 1911 that Delhi recommenced its position and the architects, Edward Lutyens and his architectures; Herbert Baker envisioned their plan to beautify the city. The finest example of their artistic approach are President House and its and adjoining buildings, projecting till today best combination of Indian, English and Roman architecture. The capital used to get shifted between Delhi and Agra during this period, afterwards the British established themselves it was removed to Calcutta.

In the modern city is full of skyscrapers, grand hotels, restaurants, shopping malls. One of posh area of Delhi Connaught Palace which was built in 1931 set the preposition for the development of the city. There is continues redevelopment and growth of the city in nearby suburb and main city. Delhi is economical hub of India and quite prominent in terms of Industrialization, Information, Investments, Science, Technology, Real Estate and Healthcare, etc. Delhi is divided in to 2 divisions, i.e., Old and New Delhi. City Old Delhi is the land of Mughals monuments, mosques and forts all through the old cluttered streets. Old bazaars and authentic food are charm of the old Delhi. Whereas New Delhi is entirely stands apart in terms of lifestyle and city's architecture, built during the British regime. New Delhi is known due to well planed specious markets, roads and landscape with greenery. Important commercial set up is situated in New Delhi's business centres like Nehru Place, Bikaji Kama, Connaught Place, ITI and South Extension. Both New and Old Delhi are quite known as tourists paradise in terms of shopping and sightseeing places, Like Rashtrapati Bhawan, India Gate, Rajghat, Qutab Minar, Humayun’s Tomb, Jantar Mantar, Purana Qila, Red Fort, Jama Masjid, Safdarjang's Tomb and Akshardham temple.

By and large Delhi is a quite multi-linguist and multi-cultured culture and society, which is now flaunting itself to embracing every old and new traditions and cultures. This is said the Delhi is the Queen of All the capital city of India.

Area: 1470 Sq.Km.

Altitude: 239 Mts

Climate:(deg C)-Summer - Max.41.2, Min.21.4, winter - Max.33.7, Min.6.8.,

Languages spoken: Hindi, English and Punjabi

Best Season to visit: September to May.

Places of Interest:

Moghul Monuments: Red Fort, Qutub Minar, Khuni Darwaza, Feroz Shah Kotla, Tughlaqabad, Nizamuddin Aulia, Humayun's Tomb, Lodi's Tomb, Safdarjung's Tomb, Jama Masjid, Jantar Mantar and Red Fort (Son-et-lumiere show).

British Monuments: India Gate, Rashtrapati Bhavan & Mughal Gardens, Parliament House, The Secretariat Complex, Teen Murti House and Connaught Place (Son-et-Lumiere show).

Excursions: Ballabgarh-36.8 kms, Badhkal Lake-32 kms,Dabchick- 92 kms, Karnalake-132 kms, Dasna- 40 kms, Dhanaa- 41 kms, Dharudara-70 kms, Hindon- 19 kms, Hodal- 90 kms, Maur Bund- 32 kms, Okhla-11 kms, Sardhana- 24 kms, Sohna-56 kms and Suraj Kund- 18 kms.

Other Monuments:Ladakh Buddha Vihar, Raj Ghat, The Supreme Court, Shanti Vana, Vijay Ghat, , Bahai’s temple, Vigyan Bhavan, Diplomatic Enclave.

Reach:

By Air: Delhi is well connected by air with all major and A class cities in India.

By Rail: Well connected with all major towns.

By Road: Agra: 204 kms, Jaipur: 260 kms, Almora: 375 kms, Khajuraho: 596 kms, Kullu: 502 kms, Shrinagar: 876 kms, Mathura-147 kms, Mussourie- 269 kms, Nainital-318 kms, Shimla -343 kms, Udaipur-663 kms.

Delhi, the towering capital city of the independent and largest democratic country in the world: India.

Delhi is located and sprawled on both banks of Yamuna River. The city is enriched with culture, architecture and human diversity, Delhi city is a blend of the ancient past of India with the vibration of the modern world. The city designed by the British architect Sir Edwin Lutyens (1869-1944) & is tree- lined & spacious. Legend has it that the Pandavas of epic Mahabharata, the august heroes, founded Delhi around 1200 BC & the name of the city was Indraprastha.

After breakfast take a sightseeing tour of Old Delhi : visiting at Rajghat, the memorial of Mahatma Gandhi, where he was cremated. The sightseeing continues to explore New Delhi: Visiting India Gate; built to honour and pay a tribute to the Indian soldiers who sacrificed themselves during the Afghan war, Birla Mandir (Laxmi Narayan Temple), Lotus shaped Bhai’s Temple, Qutub Minar; built by Qutub-ud- din Aibek of the Slave Dynasty. Later visit to Chattarpur Temple:

dedicated to the goddess Katyayani. The entire complex of the temple is spread over a wide area of 28 hectares. In the evening - visit most famous Swaminarayan Akshardham Temple, 'Akshardham' means the divine abode of God. Showcasing 10000 years of Indian culture in all its breath-taking grandeur, beauty, wisdom and bliss. If time permits optionally, you can attend the Light and Sound show in the temple complex. After visit return to the hotel for dinner and overnight stay.

Services: Hotel accommodation with breakfast and dinner, transportation for sightseeing with guide.

The Akshardham temple , which attracts approximately 70 % of all tourists who visit Delhi, it is the largest Hindu temple after the Akshardham in Gandhinagar both inspired and developed by Pramukh Swami Maharaj, the spiritual head of the Bochasanwasi Shri Akshar Purushottam Swaminarayan Sanstha, whose 3,000 volunteers helped 7,000 artisans construct the temple. Musical fountain Known as the Yagnapurush Kund, it is India's largest step well.

After breakfast check out the hotel and drive to Haridwar, on arrival transfer to the hotel. After relaxation, in the evening attend the most speculative “Ganga Aarti” at the holy River Ganga. Aarti takes place on the ghat in the evening after sunset. A group of Brahmans hold huge fire bowls in their hands and offer their holy mantras to river Ganges, Shiva - the Hindu God of destruction, Surya - the Sun God and the entire Universe. The scenario at Har - Ki - Pauri at the time of Ganga-Aarti is mesmerizing. Afterwards return to the hotel for dinner and overnight stay.

Services: Breakfast at Delhi hotel and Haridwar hotel with dinner, transportation for Ganga Aarti: Guide is not required.

Haridwar: ‘The gateway to the Gods'. \"This place is very beautiful\", at one site one will say so and fall in love with the scenic beauty of the blend of height and plains. In its long history back to pre-historic time, the Haridwar got its name from the rishis. According to the mythology it is known as Kapilsthan, legend goes that the Suryavnshi Prince Bhagirath performed penance here to salvage the souls of his ancestors who had perished due to the curse of the sage Kapila. The penance was answered and the river Ganga trickled forth from Lord Shiva's locks and its bountiful waters revived the sixty thousand sons of King Sagara. Mythologically, drops of nectar churned out from the primordial ocean fell at the four sites of the Kumbh mela including Haridwar.

Today early morning you may opt to take holy dip in Ganga, thereafter return to the hotel for breakfast. Later take a religious and spiritual sightseeing tour of Haridwar and Rishikesh. Visiting Mansa Devi Temple and if time permits visit to Chandidevi Temple: one of the most popular and most visited temples of Haridwar, thereafter

take an excursion to Rishikesh- on the way stop over at Bharat Mata Temple and Laxman Jhoola, on arrival visit Parmath Niketan and Triveni Ghat, if time permits - Gita Bhawan Ashram, afterward drive back to Haridwar for dinner and overnight stay.

Services: Hotel accommodation with breakfast and dinner, transportation for sightseeing with guide .

Rishikesh , also known as the 'place of sages' is Haridwar, at the confluence of the Chandrabhaga and Ganga. It is believed that God by the name of 'Hrishikesh' had appeared as and answers to the hard penances by Rabhiya Rishi and henceforth the place derived its name. It is most ideal destinations for meditation, yoga and other aspects of Hinduism. For the adventure seekers, Rishikesh is the suggested place for starting their trekking expeditions to the Himalayan peaks and for rafting. Also, International Yoga Week, which attracts participation from across the world, is held here, every year, in February on the banks of the Ganga.

Today morning after early breakfast, check out the hotel and drive to Mathura on arrival check into the hotel. After relaxation, in the evening visit the most prominent temple of Mathura: Krishna Janam Bhoomi (Janamshtan – Birth Place) Temple: It is built around the prison cell in which Lord Krishna’s parents; mother Devaki and father Vasudeva were imprisoned by his evil uncle Kansa. If time permits you can visit to Kansa Fort (Kans Qila). Later visit to ISKCON temple for darshan and kirtan. Afterwards return to the hotel for dinner and overnight stay.

Services: Breakfast at Haridwar Hotel, Mathura Hotel with dinner, transportation for sightseeing with guide in Mathura.

Mathura and Vrindavan , twin cities in Uttar Pradesh, India, are revered as the land of Lord Krishna's birth and childhood, making them a major pilgrimage destination for Hindus. Mathura is known as Krishna's birthplace, while Vrindavan is where he spent his childhood, playing with friends and engaging in divine pastimes. A trip to Mathura-Vrindavan offers a blend of spiritual experiences, historical sites, and cultural immersion. The notable and most popular sightseeing places and temples are Krishna Janam Bhoomi Temple, Prem Mandir, Banke Bihar Temple, ISKCON Temple, Nidhivan.

Today early in the morning visit world’s most popular and beautiful monument: Taj Mahal with its’ fabulous view at the time of sunrise. Taj Mahal, a beautiful architectural monument is one of the 7 wonders of the world. Afterwards return to the hotel for breakfast, later tour continues with a visit to Agra Fort . The built by Mughal Emperor Akbar, here you will find the splendid Pearl Mosque and various other classic example of architecture. Afterwards drive to Jaipur, if time permits - enroute stop over at Fatehpur Sikri, the old deserted town of the Mughal kingdom; it is an example of robust stability combined with originality and known for one of the largest and tallest gateways in the world . Later continue drive to Jaipur. On arrival, transfer to the hotel. After relaxation, enjoy evening at most popular Enjoy the evening at the most authentic and ethnic village resort: called Chokhi Dhani (around 15kms from the city centre) designed on the theme of an ethnic village of Rajasthan with lots of traditional environment with entertainment like folk dances, puppet shows, astrology, music, camel ride, here you can enjoy the traditional Rajasthani food. Afterwards return back to hotel for overnight stay.

Services: Breakfast at Agra Hotel, Jaipur hotel without dinner: Dinner at Chokhi Dhani. transportation for sightseeing with guide at Agra & Fatehpur Sikri. Guide is not required during visit at Chokhi Dhani.

Jaipur is widely known as the ‘Pink City’ of India. The walls, houses and buildings of the entire city were washed with pink colour for a grand and royal welcome of Prince Albert and Queen Victoria of Britain, who visited Jaipur in 1853 A.D. This splendid city as was founded in 1727 A.D by one of the greatest ruler Jai Singh II. Jaipur is surrounded by hills on three sides. Jaipur is the only city in the world, which is designed in accordance with Hindu architectural science called Shilpa Shastra. The city had been designed in rectangular shape of 9 blocks, depicting the 9 partitions of the universe. This fascinating city houses - majestic forts, grand palaces, lavish gardens, havelis and museums. While visiting these places you will have a true vision of the royal golden past of Rajasthan.

Today early morning, check out the hotel and transfer to the Jaipur Airport to board Indigo flight 6E5362 for Chennai, departing at 9.55 hrs , assistance on arrival at Chennai Airport at 12.35 hrs and transfer to the hotel. Chennai (Madras): the capital of the state of Tamil Nadu is the most convenient point of entry for the state. Chennai has an international airport, a seaport, a rail and road network that links it to all major towns and cities of the region. Tamil Nadu is a bastion of Hinduism, whose past endures into the present. Temples with towering spires called gopurams are a common feature of this state, seldom seen anywhere else in the country. Temples in Tamil Nadu were the fulcrums of society and even today art forms that find their origin in religious worship continue to colour daily life. Notable among these are splendid bronzes of deities, glass paintings and Bharatnatyam - an evocative dance form.

Today morning, after breakfast check out the Chennai hotel and drive to Mahabalipuram (60 kms: 1 ½ hr) the ancient city is situated on the shore of Bay of Bengal, famous for Its stone carvings, this UNESCO World Heritage Site Has Many Rock-cut Monuments Dating from 7th – 9th Century, here you can visit to Shore Temples and Seashore Beach, Pancha Rathas, Arjuna's Penance, Mahishasurmardini Cave and panoramic view of Light house. Afterwards proceed to Kanchipuram (50 kms: 1 ½ hr) to explore the ancient capital of the Pallavas famous, here visit the most famous temple of Lord Shiva: Kailasanathar; built during 685 A.D. to 705 A.D. Later you must visit at the world-famous SILK CLOTH MARKET for shopping of silk sarees, clothes and other handicraft product. Afterwards continue to proceed to

Tirupati (120 kms: 2-3 hrs from Kanchipuram), on arrival transfer to the hotel for dinner and overnight at Tirupati.

Services: Breakfast at Chennai hotel, Transportation and guide services at Mahabalipuram and Kanchipuram.

Tirupati hotel with dinner. Transportation for Tirupati, no guide is required in Tirupati.

Mahabalipuram with its picturesque location on a rocky outcrop between the beach and a lagoon is a happy combination of history, good beaches, hassle-free tourism, fabulous fish and lobster! Despite the many visitors, drawn by the former Pallava dynasty town, the place is friendly, relaxed, and the villagers are remarkably unperturbed by their crowds of visitors. Mahabalipuram is renowned for its series of charming rathas and the spectacular carved relic depicting Arjuna's Penance. The magnificent Shore Temple, built by King Rajasimha in the seventh century, is a unique temple that houses the shrines of both Shiva and Vishnu while the Varaha Cave is one of the many rock-cut caves in Mahabalipuram. The Krishna Mandapam has a relic of Lord Krishna lifting the Govardhan hill in his fingertips.

Kanchipuram is known as one of India's Seven Sacred cities and the historical capital of the Pallavas. It was under the Pallavas from 6th to 8th century A.D and later became the citadel of Cholas, Vijayanagar Kings, the Muslim and the British. It has been a centre of Tamil learning, cultural and religious background for centuries. Kanchi is also known as the centre of the finest silk sarees made in the country. Kanchi has magnificent temples of unique architectural beauty bearing eloquent testimony to its glorious Dravidian heritage. Adi Sankara established his Episcopal seat (Kamakotipeetam) here in the city. The city is also the birthplace of C.N. Annadurai, former Chief Minister of Tamil Nadu affectionately called as \"Anna\" by the people of Tamil Nadu.

Today early morning visit for morning prayers of Lord Balaji - The crown jewel of Tirumala, this opulent temple is dedicated to Lord Vishnu. Witness the ornate architecture, intricate carvings, and experience the awe-inspiring darshan (holy visit) of the revered Tirupati Balaji, if time permits visit at Padmavati Lakshmi Mandir and Sri Anjaneyaswami Temple. Later return to the hotel, after relaxation check out the hotel and transfer to Tirupati Airport to board the Air India Flight AI 2890 departing for Delhi at 1510 hrs, oscitance on arrival at Delhi at 1955 hrs. Check into the hotel. Dinner and overnight at the hotel in Delhi.

Services: Breakfast at Tirupati hotel, Tirupati Temple visit of your own, guides are now allowed, transportation for airport transfer at Tirupati and Delhi.

The Tirumala Hills are part of Seshachalam Hills range. The hills are 853m above sea level. The Hills comprises seven peaks, representing the seven heads of Adisesha. The temple lies on the seventh peak - Venkatadri, on the southern banks of Sri Swami Pushkarini, a holy water tank. Hence the temple is also referred to as \"Temple of Seven Hills\". Tirupati’s presiding deity; Lord Venkateswara, is famous all over the world as the giver of boons, and is paid homage by people across all religions and races. The Temple is dedicated to Lord Venkateswara, an incarnation of Vishnu, who is believed to have appeared here to

save mankind from trials and troubles of Kali Yuga.

Services: Hotel accommodation with dinner and transportation for transfer.

Delhi, the towering capital city of the independent and largest democratic country in the world: India.

Delhi is located and sprawled on both banks of Yamuna River. The city is enriched with culture, architecture and human diversity, Delhi city is a blend of the ancient past of India with the vibration of the modern world. The city designed by the British architect Sir Edwin Lutyens (1869-1944) & is tree- lined & spacious. Legend has it that the Pandavas of epic Mahabharata, the august heroes, founded Delhi around 1200 BC & the name of the city was Indraprastha.

After breakfast take a sightseeing tour of Old Delhi : visiting at Rajghat, the memorial of Mahatma Gandhi, where he was cremated. The sightseeing continues to explore New Delhi: Visiting India Gate; built to honour and pay a tribute to the Indian soldiers who sacrificed themselves during the Afghan war, Birla Mandir (Laxmi Narayan Temple), Lotus shaped Bhai’s Temple, Qutub Minar; built by Qutub-ud- din Aibek of the Slave Dynasty. Later visit to Chattarpur Temple:

dedicated to the goddess Katyayani. The entire complex of the temple is spread over a wide area of 28 hectares. In the evening - visit most famous Swaminarayan Akshardham Temple, 'Akshardham' means the divine abode of God. Showcasing 10000 years of Indian culture in all its breath-taking grandeur, beauty, wisdom and bliss. If time permits optionally, you can attend the Light and Sound show in the temple complex. After visit return to the hotel for dinner and overnight stay.

Services: Hotel accommodation with breakfast and dinner, transportation for sightseeing with guide.

The Akshardham temple , which attracts approximately 70 % of all tourists who visit Delhi, it is the largest Hindu temple after the Akshardham in Gandhinagar both inspired and developed by Pramukh Swami Maharaj, the spiritual head of the Bochasanwasi Shri Akshar Purushottam Swaminarayan Sanstha, whose 3,000 volunteers helped 7,000 artisans construct the temple. Musical fountain Known as the Yagnapurush Kund, it is India's largest step well.

After breakfast check out the hotel and drive to Haridwar, on arrival transfer to the hotel. After relaxation, in the evening attend the most speculative “Ganga Aarti” at the holy River Ganga. Aarti takes place on the ghat in the evening after sunset. A group of Brahmans hold huge fire bowls in their hands and offer their holy mantras to river Ganges, Shiva - the Hindu God of destruction, Surya - the Sun God and the entire Universe. The scenario at Har - Ki - Pauri at the time of Ganga-Aarti is mesmerizing. Afterwards return to the hotel for dinner and overnight stay.

Services: Breakfast at Delhi hotel and Haridwar hotel with dinner, transportation for Ganga Aarti: Guide is not required.

Haridwar: ‘The gateway to the Gods'. \"This place is very beautiful\", at one site one will say so and fall in love with the scenic beauty of the blend of height and plains. In its long history back to pre-historic time, the Haridwar got its name from the rishis. According to the mythology it is known as Kapilsthan, legend goes that the Suryavnshi Prince Bhagirath performed penance here to salvage the souls of his ancestors who had perished due to the curse of the sage Kapila. The penance was answered and the river Ganga trickled forth from Lord Shiva's locks and its bountiful waters revived the sixty thousand sons of King Sagara. Mythologically, drops of nectar churned out from the primordial ocean fell at the four sites of the Kumbh mela including Haridwar.

Today early morning you may opt to take holy dip in Ganga, thereafter return to the hotel for breakfast. Later take a religious and spiritual sightseeing tour of Haridwar and Rishikesh. Visiting Mansa Devi Temple and if time permits visit to Chandidevi Temple: one of the most popular and most visited temples of Haridwar, thereafter

take an excursion to Rishikesh- on the way stop over at Bharat Mata Temple and Laxman Jhoola, on arrival visit Parmath Niketan and Triveni Ghat, if time permits - Gita Bhawan Ashram, afterward drive back to Haridwar for dinner and overnight stay.

Services: Hotel accommodation with breakfast and dinner, transportation for sightseeing with guide .

Rishikesh , also known as the 'place of sages' is Haridwar, at the confluence of the Chandrabhaga and Ganga. It is believed that God by the name of 'Hrishikesh' had appeared as and answers to the hard penances by Rabhiya Rishi and henceforth the place derived its name. It is most ideal destinations for meditation, yoga and other aspects of Hinduism. For the adventure seekers, Rishikesh is the suggested place for starting their trekking expeditions to the Himalayan peaks and for rafting. Also, International Yoga Week, which attracts participation from across the world, is held here, every year, in February on the banks of the Ganga.

Mathura and Vrindavan , twin cities in Uttar Pradesh, India, are revered as the land of Lord Krishna's birth and childhood, making them a major pilgrimage destination for Hindus. Mathura is known as Krishna's birthplace, while Vrindavan is where he spent his childhood, playing with friends and engaging in divine pastimes. A trip to Mathura-Vrindavan offers a blend of spiritual experiences, historical sites, and cultural immersion. The notable and most popular sightseeing places and temples are Krishna Janam Bhoomi Temple, Prem Mandir, Banke Bihar Temple, ISKCON Temple, Nidhivan.

Jaipur is widely known as the ‘Pink City’ of India. The walls, houses and buildings of the entire city were washed with pink colour for a grand and royal welcome of Prince Albert and Queen Victoria of Britain, who visited Jaipur in 1853 A.D. This splendid city as was founded in 1727 A.D by one of the greatest ruler Jai Singh II. Jaipur is surrounded by hills on three sides. Jaipur is the only city in the world, which is designed in accordance with Hindu architectural science called Shilpa Shastra. The city had been designed in rectangular shape of 9 blocks, depicting the 9 partitions of the universe. This fascinating city houses - majestic forts, grand palaces, lavish gardens, havelis and museums. While visiting these places you will have a true vision of the royal golden past of Rajasthan.

Chennai (Madras): the capital of the state of Tamil Nadu is the most convenient point of entry for the state. Chennai has an international airport, a seaport, a rail and road network that links it to all major towns and cities of the region. Tamil Nadu is a bastion of Hinduism, whose past endures into the present. Temples with towering spires called gopurams are a common feature of this state, seldom seen anywhere else in the country. Temples in Tamil Nadu were the fulcrums of society and even today art forms that find their origin in religious worship continue to colour daily life. Notable among these are splendid bronzes of deities, glass paintings and Bharatnatyam - an evocative dance form.

Today morning, after breakfast check out the Chennai hotel and drive to Mahabalipuram (60 kms: 1 ½ hr) the ancient city is situated on the shore of Bay of Bengal, famous for Its stone carvings, this UNESCO World Heritage Site Has Many Rock-cut Monuments Dating from 7th – 9th Century, here you can visit to Shore Temples and Seashore Beach, Pancha Rathas, Arjuna's Penance, Mahishasurmardini Cave and panoramic view of Light house. Afterwards proceed to Kanchipuram (50 kms: 1 ½ hr) to explore the ancient capital of the Pallavas famous, here visit the most famous temple of Lord Shiva: Kailasanathar; built during 685 A.D. to 705 A.D. Tirupati hotel with dinner. Transportation for Tirupati, no guide is required in Tirupati.

Mahabalipuram with its picturesque location on a rocky outcrop between the beach and a lagoon is a happy combination of history, good beaches, hassle-free tourism, fabulous fish and lobster! Despite the many visitors, drawn by the former Pallava dynasty town, the place is friendly, relaxed, and the villagers are remarkably unperturbed by their crowds of visitors. Mahabalipuram is renowned for its series of charming rathas and the spectacular carved relic depicting Arjuna's Penance. The magnificent Shore Temple, built by King Rajasimha in the seventh century, is a unique temple that houses the shrines of both Shiva and Vishnu while the Varaha Cave is one of the many rock-cut caves in Mahabalipuram. The Krishna Mandapam has a relic of Lord Krishna lifting the Govardhan hill in his fingertips.

Kanchipuram is known as one of India's Seven Sacred cities and the historical capital of the Pallavas. It was under the Pallavas from 6th to 8th century A.D and later became the citadel of Cholas, Vijayanagar Kings, the Muslim and the British. It has been a centre of Tamil learning, cultural and religious background for centuries. Kanchi is also known as the centre of the finest silk sarees made in the country. Kanchi has magnificent temples of unique architectural beauty bearing eloquent testimony to its glorious Dravidian heritage. Adi Sankara established his Episcopal seat (Kamakotipeetam) here in the city. The city is also the birthplace of C.N. Annadurai, former Chief Minister of Tamil Nadu affectionately called as \"Anna\" by the people of Tamil Nadu.

The Tirumala Hills are part of Seshachalam Hills range. The hills are 853m above sea level. The Hills comprises seven peaks, representing the seven heads of Adisesha. The temple lies on the seventh peak - Venkatadri, on the southern banks of Sri Swami Pushkarini, a holy water tank. Hence the temple is also referred to as \"Temple of Seven Hills\". Tirupati’s presiding deity; Lord Venkateswara, is famous all over the world as the giver of boons, and is paid homage by people across all religions and races. The Temple is dedicated to Lord Venkateswara, an incarnation of Vishnu, who is believed to have appeared here to

save mankind from trials and troubles of Kali Yuga.

Delhi, the towering capital city of the independent and largest democratic country in the world: India.

Delhi is located and sprawled on both banks of Yamuna River. The city is enriched with culture, architecture and human diversity, Delhi city is a blend of the ancient past of India with the vibration of the modern world. The city designed by the British architect Sir Edwin Lutyens (1869-1944) & is tree- lined & spacious. Legend has it that the Pandavas of epic Mahabharata, the august heroes, founded Delhi around 1200 BC & the name of the city was Indraprastha.

After breakfast take a sightseeing tour of Old Delhi : visiting at Rajghat, the memorial of Mahatma Gandhi, where he was cremated. The sightseeing continues to explore New Delhi: Visiting India Gate; built to honour and pay a tribute to the Indian soldiers who sacrificed themselves during the Afghan war, Birla Mandir (Laxmi Narayan Temple), Lotus shaped Bhai’s Temple, Qutub Minar; built by Qutub-ud- din Aibek of the Slave Dynasty. Later visit to Chattarpur Temple:

dedicated to the goddess Katyayani. The entire complex of the temple is spread over a wide area of 28 hectares. In the evening - visit most famous Swaminarayan Akshardham Temple, 'Akshardham' means the divine abode of God. Showcasing 10000 years of Indian culture in all its breath-taking grandeur, beauty, wisdom and bliss. If time permits optionally, you can attend the Light and Sound show in the temple complex. After visit return to the hotel for dinner and overnight stay.

Services: Hotel accommodation with breakfast and dinner, transportation for sightseeing with guide.

The Akshardham temple , which attracts approximately 70 % of all tourists who visit Delhi, it is the largest Hindu temple after the Akshardham in Gandhinagar both inspired and developed by Pramukh Swami Maharaj, the spiritual head of the Bochasanwasi Shri Akshar Purushottam Swaminarayan Sanstha, whose 3,000 volunteers helped 7,000 artisans construct the temple. Musical fountain Known as the Yagnapurush Kund, it is India's largest step well.

After breakfast check out the hotel and drive to Haridwar, on arrival transfer to the hotel. After relaxation, in the evening attend the most speculative “Ganga Aarti” at the holy River Ganga. Aarti takes place on the ghat in the evening after sunset. A group of Brahmans hold huge fire bowls in their hands and offer their holy mantras to river Ganges, Shiva - the Hindu God of destruction, Surya - the Sun God and the entire Universe. The scenario at Har - Ki - Pauri at the time of Ganga-Aarti is mesmerizing. Afterwards return to the hotel for dinner and overnight stay.

Services: Breakfast at Delhi hotel and Haridwar hotel with dinner, transportation for Ganga Aarti: Guide is not required.

Haridwar: ‘The gateway to the Gods'. \"This place is very beautiful\", at one site one will say so and fall in love with the scenic beauty of the blend of height and plains. In its long history back to pre-historic time, the Haridwar got its name from the rishis. According to the mythology it is known as Kapilsthan, legend goes that the Suryavnshi Prince Bhagirath performed penance here to salvage the souls of his ancestors who had perished due to the curse of the sage Kapila. The penance was answered and the river Ganga trickled forth from Lord Shiva's locks and its bountiful waters revived the sixty thousand sons of King Sagara. Mythologically, drops of nectar churned out from the primordial ocean fell at the four sites of the Kumbh mela including Haridwar.

Today early morning you may opt to take holy dip in Ganga, thereafter return to the hotel for breakfast. Later take a religious and spiritual sightseeing tour of Haridwar and Rishikesh. Visiting Mansa Devi Temple and if time permits visit to Chandidevi Temple: one of the most popular and most visited temples of Haridwar, thereafter

take an excursion to Rishikesh- on the way stop over at Bharat Mata Temple and Laxman Jhoola, on arrival visit Parmath Niketan and Triveni Ghat, if time permits - Gita Bhawan Ashram, afterward drive back to Haridwar for dinner and overnight stay.

Services: Hotel accommodation with breakfast and dinner, transportation for sightseeing with guide .

Rishikesh , also known as the 'place of sages' is Haridwar, at the confluence of the Chandrabhaga and Ganga. It is believed that God by the name of 'Hrishikesh' had appeared as and answers to the hard penances by Rabhiya Rishi and henceforth the place derived its name. It is most ideal destinations for meditation, yoga and other aspects of Hinduism. For the adventure seekers, Rishikesh is the suggested place for starting their trekking expeditions to the Himalayan peaks and for rafting. Also, International Yoga Week, which attracts participation from across the world, is held here, every year, in February on the banks of the Ganga.

Today morning after early breakfast, check out the hotel and drive to Mathura on arrival check into the hotel. After relaxation, in the evening visit the most prominent temple of Mathura: Krishna Janam Bhoomi (Janamshtan – Birth Place) Temple: It is built around the prison cell in which Lord Krishna’s parents; mother Devaki and father Vasudeva were imprisoned by his evil uncle Kansa. If time permits you can visit to Kansa Fort (Kans Qila). Later visit to ISKCON temple for darshan and kirtan. Afterwards return to the hotel for dinner and overnight stay.

Services: Breakfast at Haridwar Hotel, Mathura Hotel with dinner, transportation for sightseeing with guide in Mathura.

Mathura and Vrindavan , twin cities in Uttar Pradesh, India, are revered as the land of Lord Krishna's birth and childhood, making them a major pilgrimage destination for Hindus. Mathura is known as Krishna's birthplace, while Vrindavan is where he spent his childhood, playing with friends and engaging in divine pastimes. A trip to Mathura-Vrindavan offers a blend of spiritual experiences, historical sites, and cultural immersion. The notable and most popular sightseeing places and temples are Krishna Janam Bhoomi Temple, Prem Mandir, Banke Bihar Temple, ISKCON Temple, Nidhivan.

Today early in the morning visit world’s most popular and beautiful monument: Taj Mahal with its’ fabulous view at the time of sunrise. Taj Mahal, a beautiful architectural monument is one of the 7 wonders of the world. Afterwards return to the hotel for breakfast, later tour continues with a visit to Agra Fort . The built by Mughal Emperor Akbar, here you will find the splendid Pearl Mosque and various other classic example of architecture. Afterwards drive to Jaipur, if time permits - enroute stop over at Fatehpur Sikri, the old deserted town of the Mughal kingdom; it is an example of robust stability combined with originality and known for one of the largest and tallest gateways in the world . After relaxation, enjoy evening at most popular Enjoy the evening at the most authentic and ethnic village resort: called Chokhi Dhani (around 15kms from the city centre) designed on the theme of an ethnic village of Rajasthan with lots of traditional environment with entertainment like folk dances, puppet shows, astrology, music, camel ride, here you can enjoy the traditional Rajasthani food. Afterwards return back to hotel for overnight stay.

Services: Breakfast at Agra Hotel, Jaipur hotel without dinner: Dinner at Chokhi Dhani. transportation for sightseeing with guide at Agra & Fatehpur Sikri. Guide is not required during visit at Chokhi Dhani.

Jaipur is widely known as the ‘Pink City’ of India. The walls, houses and buildings of the entire city were washed with pink colour for a grand and royal welcome of Prince Albert and Queen Victoria of Britain, who visited Jaipur in 1853 A.D. This splendid city as was founded in 1727 A.D by one of the greatest ruler Jai Singh II. Jaipur is surrounded by hills on three sides. Jaipur is the only city in the world, which is designed in accordance with Hindu architectural science called Shilpa Shastra. The city had been designed in rectangular shape of 9 blocks, depicting the 9 partitions of the universe. This fascinating city houses - majestic forts, grand palaces, lavish gardens, havelis and museums. While visiting these places you will have a true vision of the royal golden past of Rajasthan.

Chennai (Madras): the capital of the state of Tamil Nadu is the most convenient point of entry for the state. Chennai has an international airport, a seaport, a rail and road network that links it to all major towns and cities of the region. Tamil Nadu is a bastion of Hinduism, whose past endures into the present. Temples with towering spires called gopurams are a common feature of this state, seldom seen anywhere else in the country. Temples in Tamil Nadu were the fulcrums of society and even today art forms that find their origin in religious worship continue to colour daily life. Notable among these are splendid bronzes of deities, glass paintings and Bharatnatyam - an evocative dance form.

If time permits you can visit local market for shopping, then return to the hotel for dinner and overnight stay at Chennai.","bold":false}],[{"text":"Services: Jaipur hotel breakfast if time permits, Chennai Hotel with dinner, transportation for sightseeing with guide in Chennai.","bold":false}],[{"text":"Chennai (Madras): the capital of the state of Tamil Nadu is the most convenient point of entry for the state. Chennai has an international airport, a seaport, a rail and road network that links it to all major towns and cities of the region. Tamil Nadu is a bastion of Hinduism, whose past endures into the present. Temples with towering spires called gopurams are a common feature of this state, seldom seen anywhere else in the country. Temples in Tamil Nadu were the fulcrums of society and even today art forms that find their origin in religious worship continue to colour daily life. Notable among these are splendid bronzes of deities, glass paintings and Bharatnatyam - an evocative dance form.","bold":false}],[{"text":"rd","bold":false}]]},{"day":"10 Day","title":"23 Nov: (Mon) Chennai- Mahabalipuram-Kanchipuram- Tirupati","eta":"230 kms: 4-5 hours","photo":"","note":"","html":"

Today morning, after breakfast check out the Chennai hotel and drive to Mahabalipuram (60 kms: 1 ½ hr) the ancient city is situated on the shore of Bay of Bengal, famous for Its stone carvings, this UNESCO World Heritage Site Has Many Rock-cut Monuments Dating from 7th – 9th Century, here you can visit to Shore Temples and Seashore Beach, Pancha Rathas, Arjuna's Penance, Mahishasurmardini Cave and panoramic view of Light house. Afterwards proceed to Kanchipuram (50 kms: 1 ½ hr) to explore the ancient capital of the Pallavas famous, here visit the most famous temple of Lord Shiva: Kailasanathar; built during 685 A.D. to 705 A.D. Later you must visit at the world-famous SILK CLOTH MARKET for shopping of silk sarees, clothes and other handicraft product. Afterwards continue to proceed to

Tirupati (120 kms: 2-3 hrs from Kanchipuram), on arrival transfer to the hotel for dinner and overnight at Tirupati.

Services: Breakfast at Chennai hotel, Transportation and guide services at Mahabalipuram and Kanchipuram.

Tirupati hotel with dinner. Transportation for Tirupati, no guide is required in Tirupati.

Mahabalipuram with its picturesque location on a rocky outcrop between the beach and a lagoon is a happy combination of history, good beaches, hassle-free tourism, fabulous fish and lobster! Despite the many visitors, drawn by the former Pallava dynasty town, the place is friendly, relaxed, and the villagers are remarkably unperturbed by their crowds of visitors. Mahabalipuram is renowned for its series of charming rathas and the spectacular carved relic depicting Arjuna's Penance. The magnificent Shore Temple, built by King Rajasimha in the seventh century, is a unique temple that houses the shrines of both Shiva and Vishnu while the Varaha Cave is one of the many rock-cut caves in Mahabalipuram. The Krishna Mandapam has a relic of Lord Krishna lifting the Govardhan hill in his fingertips.

Kanchipuram is known as one of India's Seven Sacred cities and the historical capital of the Pallavas. It was under the Pallavas from 6th to 8th century A.D and later became the citadel of Cholas, Vijayanagar Kings, the Muslim and the British. It has been a centre of Tamil learning, cultural and religious background for centuries. Kanchi is also known as the centre of the finest silk sarees made in the country. Kanchi has magnificent temples of unique architectural beauty bearing eloquent testimony to its glorious Dravidian heritage. Adi Sankara established his Episcopal seat (Kamakotipeetam) here in the city. The city is also the birthplace of C.N. Annadurai, former Chief Minister of Tamil Nadu affectionately called as \"Anna\" by the people of Tamil Nadu.

Today early morning visit for morning prayers of Lord Balaji - The crown jewel of Tirumala, this opulent temple is dedicated to Lord Vishnu. Witness the ornate architecture, intricate carvings, and experience the awe-inspiring darshan (holy visit) of the revered Tirupati Balaji, if time permits visit at Padmavati Lakshmi Mandir and Sri Anjaneyaswami Temple. Later return to the hotel, after relaxation check out the hotel and transfer to Tirupati Airport to board the Air India Flight AI 2890 departing for Delhi at 1510 hrs, oscitance on arrival at Delhi at 1955 hrs. Check into the hotel. Dinner and overnight at the hotel in Delhi.

Services: Breakfast at Tirupati hotel, Tirupati Temple visit of your own, guides are now allowed, transportation for airport transfer at Tirupati and Delhi.

The Tirumala Hills are part of Seshachalam Hills range. The hills are 853m above sea level. The Hills comprises seven peaks, representing the seven heads of Adisesha. The temple lies on the seventh peak - Venkatadri, on the southern banks of Sri Swami Pushkarini, a holy water tank. Hence the temple is also referred to as \"Temple of Seven Hills\". Tirupati’s presiding deity; Lord Venkateswara, is famous all over the world as the giver of boons, and is paid homage by people across all religions and races. The Temple is dedicated to Lord Venkateswara, an incarnation of Vishnu, who is believed to have appeared here to

save mankind from trials and troubles of Kali Yuga.

Delhi, the towering capital city of the independent and largest democratic country in the world: India.

Delhi is located and sprawled on both banks of Yamuna River. The city is enriched with culture, architecture and human diversity, Delhi city is a blend of the ancient past of India with the vibration of the modern world. The city designed by the British architect Sir Edwin Lutyens (1869-1944) & is tree- lined & spacious. Legend has it that the Pandavas of epic Mahabharata, the august heroes, founded Delhi around 1200 BC & the name of the city was Indraprastha.

After breakfast take a sightseeing tour of Old Delhi : visiting at Rajghat, the memorial of Mahatma Gandhi, where he was cremated. The sightseeing continues to explore New Delhi: Visiting India Gate; built to honour and pay a tribute to the Indian soldiers who sacrificed themselves during the Afghan war, Birla Mandir (Laxmi Narayan Temple), Lotus shaped Bhai’s Temple, Qutub Minar; built by Qutub-ud- din Aibek of the Slave Dynasty. Later visit to Chattarpur Temple:

dedicated to the goddess Katyayani. The entire complex of the temple is spread over a wide area of 28 hectares. In the evening - visit most famous Swaminarayan Akshardham Temple, 'Akshardham' means the divine abode of God. Showcasing 10000 years of Indian culture in all its breath-taking grandeur, beauty, wisdom and bliss. If time permits optionally, you can attend the Light and Sound show in the temple complex. After visit return to the hotel for dinner and overnight stay.

Services: Hotel accommodation with breakfast and dinner, transportation for sightseeing with guide.

The Akshardham temple , which attracts approximately 70 % of all tourists who visit Delhi, it is the largest Hindu temple after the Akshardham in Gandhinagar both inspired and developed by Pramukh Swami Maharaj, the spiritual head of the Bochasanwasi Shri Akshar Purushottam Swaminarayan Sanstha, whose 3,000 volunteers helped 7,000 artisans construct the temple. Musical fountain Known as the Yagnapurush Kund, it is India's largest step well.

After breakfast check out the hotel and drive to Haridwar, on arrival transfer to the hotel. After relaxation, in the evening attend the most speculative “Ganga Aarti” at the holy River Ganga. Aarti takes place on the ghat in the evening after sunset. A group of Brahmans hold huge fire bowls in their hands and offer their holy mantras to river Ganges, Shiva - the Hindu God of destruction, Surya - the Sun God and the entire Universe. The scenario at Har - Ki - Pauri at the time of Ganga-Aarti is mesmerizing. Afterwards return to the hotel for dinner and overnight stay.

Services: Breakfast at Delhi hotel and Haridwar hotel with dinner, transportation for Ganga Aarti: Guide is not required.

Haridwar: ‘The gateway to the Gods'. \"This place is very beautiful\", at one site one will say so and fall in love with the scenic beauty of the blend of height and plains. In its long history back to pre-historic time, the Haridwar got its name from the rishis. According to the mythology it is known as Kapilsthan, legend goes that the Suryavnshi Prince Bhagirath performed penance here to salvage the souls of his ancestors who had perished due to the curse of the sage Kapila. The penance was answered and the river Ganga trickled forth from Lord Shiva's locks and its bountiful waters revived the sixty thousand sons of King Sagara. Mythologically, drops of nectar churned out from the primordial ocean fell at the four sites of the Kumbh mela including Haridwar.

Today early morning you may opt to take holy dip in Ganga, thereafter return to the hotel for breakfast. Later take a religious and spiritual sightseeing tour of Haridwar and Rishikesh. Visiting Mansa Devi Temple and if time permits visit to Chandidevi Temple: one of the most popular and most visited temples of Haridwar, thereafter

take an excursion to Rishikesh- on the way stop over at Bharat Mata Temple and Laxman Jhoola, on arrival visit Parmath Niketan and Triveni Ghat, if time permits - Gita Bhawan Ashram, afterward drive back to Haridwar for dinner and overnight stay.

Rishikesh , also known as the 'place of sages' is Haridwar, at the confluence of the Chandrabhaga and Ganga. It is believed that God by the name of 'Hrishikesh' had appeared as and answers to the hard penances by Rabhiya Rishi and henceforth the place derived its name. It is most ideal destinations for meditation, yoga and other aspects of Hinduism. For the adventure seekers, Rishikesh is the suggested place for starting their trekking expeditions to the Himalayan peaks and for rafting. Also, International Yoga Week, which attracts participation from across the world, is held here, every year, in February on the banks of the Ganga.

Mathura is known as Krishna's birthplace, while Vrindavan is where he spent his childhood, playing with friends and engaging in divine pastimes. A trip to Mathura-Vrindavan offers a blend of spiritual experiences, historical sites, and cultural immersion. The notable and most popular sightseeing places and temples are Krishna Janam Bhoomi Temple, Prem Mandir, Banke Bihar Temple, ISKCON Temple, Nidhivan.

Jaipur is widely known as the ‘Pink City’ of India. The walls, houses and buildings of the entire city were washed with pink colour for a grand and royal welcome of Prince Albert and Queen Victoria of Britain, who visited Jaipur in 1853 A.D. This splendid city as was founded in 1727 A.D by one of the greatest ruler Jai Singh II. Jaipur is surrounded by hills on three sides. Jaipur is the only city in the world, which is designed in accordance with Hindu architectural science called Shilpa Shastra. The city had been designed in rectangular shape of 9 blocks, depicting the 9 partitions of the universe. This fascinating city houses - majestic forts, grand palaces, lavish gardens, havelis and museums. While visiting these places you will have a true vision of the royal golden past of Rajasthan.

Chennai (Madras): the capital of the state of Tamil Nadu is the most convenient point of entry for the state. Chennai has an international airport, a seaport, a rail and road network that links it to all major towns and cities of the region. Tamil Nadu is a bastion of Hinduism, whose past endures into the present. Temples with towering spires called gopurams are a common feature of this state, seldom seen anywhere else in the country. Temples in Tamil Nadu were the fulcrums of society and even today art forms that find their origin in religious worship continue to colour daily life. Notable among these are splendid bronzes of deities, glass paintings and Bharatnatyam - an evocative dance form.

Mahabalipuram with its picturesque location on a rocky outcrop between the beach and a lagoon is a happy combination of history, good beaches, hassle-free tourism, fabulous fish and lobster! Despite the many visitors, drawn by the former Pallava dynasty town, the place is friendly, relaxed, and the villagers are remarkably unperturbed by their crowds of visitors. Mahabalipuram is renowned for its series of charming rathas and the spectacular carved relic depicting Arjuna's Penance. The magnificent Shore Temple, built by King Rajasimha in the seventh century, is a unique temple that houses the shrines of both Shiva and Vishnu while the Varaha Cave is one of the many rock-cut caves in Mahabalipuram. The Krishna Mandapam has a relic of Lord Krishna lifting the Govardhan hill in his fingertips.

Kanchipuram is known as one of India's Seven Sacred cities and the historical capital of the Pallavas. It was under the Pallavas from 6th to 8th century A.D and later became the citadel of Cholas, Vijayanagar Kings, the Muslim and the British. It has been a centre of Tamil learning, cultural and religious background for centuries. Kanchi is also known as the centre of the finest silk sarees made in the country. Kanchi has magnificent temples of unique architectural beauty bearing eloquent testimony to its glorious Dravidian heritage. Adi Sankara established his Episcopal seat (Kamakotipeetam) here in the city. The city is also the birthplace of C.N. Annadurai, former Chief Minister of Tamil Nadu affectionately called as \"Anna\" by the people of Tamil Nadu.

The Tirumala Hills are part of Seshachalam Hills range. The hills are 853m above sea level. The Hills comprises seven peaks, representing the seven heads of Adisesha. The temple lies on the seventh peak - Venkatadri, on the southern banks of Sri Swami Pushkarini, a holy water tank. Hence the temple is also referred to as \"Temple of Seven Hills\". Tirupati’s presiding deity; Lord Venkateswara, is famous all over the world as the giver of boons, and is paid homage by people across all religions and races. The Temple is dedicated to Lord Venkateswara, an incarnation of Vishnu, who is believed to have appeared here to

save mankind from trials and troubles of Kali Yuga.

Welcome at Indira Gandhi International Airport on arrival at 7.30 pm at Delhi with a PLA card of your name and transferred by a/c mini coach to the pre-booked hotel. After check in, our representative will hand over all required documents related to the tour and service and brief you about the tour - intercity travel, sightseeing places, stopovers, eating places, local SIM card, money exchange, tips etc., rest of the time for relaxation. Dinner and overnight at the hotel.

Services: Hotel accommodation with dinner and transportation for transfer.

Delhi, the towering capital city of the independent and largest democratic country in the world: India.

Delhi is located and sprawled on both banks of Yamuna River. The city is enriched with culture, architecture and human diversity, Delhi city is a blend of the ancient past of India with the vibration of the modern world. The city designed by the British architect Sir Edwin Lutyens (1869-1944) & is tree- lined & spacious. Legend has it that the Pandavas of epic Mahabharata, the august heroes, founded Delhi around 1200 BC & the name of the city was Indraprastha.

After breakfast take a sightseeing tour of Old Delhi : visiting at Rajghat, the memorial of Mahatma Gandhi, where he was cremated. The sightseeing continues to explore New Delhi: Visiting India Gate; built to honour and pay a tribute to the Indian soldiers who sacrificed themselves during the Afghan war, Birla Mandir (Laxmi Narayan Temple), Lotus shaped Bhai’s Temple, Qutub Minar; built by Qutub-ud- din Aibek of the Slave Dynasty. Later visit to Chattarpur Temple:

dedicated to the goddess Katyayani. The entire complex of the temple is spread over a wide area of 28 hectares. In the evening - visit most famous Swaminarayan Akshardham Temple, 'Akshardham' means the divine abode of God. Showcasing 10000 years of Indian culture in all its breath-taking grandeur, beauty, wisdom and bliss. If time permits optionally, you can attend the Light and Sound show in the temple complex. After visit return to the hotel for dinner and overnight stay.

Services: Hotel accommodation with breakfast and dinner, transportation for sightseeing with guide.

The Akshardham temple , which attracts approximately 70 % of all tourists who visit Delhi, it is the largest Hindu temple after the Akshardham in Gandhinagar both inspired and developed by Pramukh Swami Maharaj, the spiritual head of the Bochasanwasi Shri Akshar Purushottam Swaminarayan Sanstha, whose 3,000 volunteers helped 7,000 artisans construct the temple. Musical fountain Known as the Yagnapurush Kund, it is India's largest step well.

After breakfast check out the hotel and drive to Haridwar, on arrival transfer to the hotel. After relaxation, in the evening attend the most speculative “Ganga Aarti” at the holy River Ganga. Aarti takes place on the ghat in the evening after sunset. A group of Brahmans hold huge fire bowls in their hands and offer their holy mantras to river Ganges, Shiva - the Hindu God of destruction, Surya - the Sun God and the entire Universe. The scenario at Har - Ki - Pauri at the time of Ganga-Aarti is mesmerizing. Afterwards return to the hotel for dinner and overnight stay.

Services: Breakfast at Delhi hotel and Haridwar hotel with dinner, transportation for Ganga Aarti: Guide is not required.

Haridwar: ‘The gateway to the Gods'. \"This place is very beautiful\", at one site one will say so and fall in love with the scenic beauty of the blend of height and plains. In its long history back to pre-historic time, the Haridwar got its name from the rishis. According to the mythology it is known as Kapilsthan, legend goes that the Suryavnshi Prince Bhagirath performed penance here to salvage the souls of his ancestors who had perished due to the curse of the sage Kapila. The penance was answered and the river Ganga trickled forth from Lord Shiva's locks and its bountiful waters revived the sixty thousand sons of King Sagara. Mythologically, drops of nectar churned out from the primordial ocean fell at the four sites of the Kumbh mela including Haridwar.
